title: How to manage product images for a growing Shopify store with Photoroom
summary: Manage Shopify product images with Photoroom: edit images in bulk, create new visuals and variants, improve listings, and publish updates back to Shopify.
body_markdown:
***TL;DR: Growing Shopify stores can use Photoroom to manage product imagery and listing optimization directly from their connected catalog: edit and batch-update existing assets, generate additional product shots with AI Shot List, create imagery for Shopify variants, generate or improve product titles and descriptions, optimize image names and alt text, check Listing Score, and publish approved changes back to Shopify.***


Managing Shopify product images is simple when the catalog is small. You add a product, edit its images, upload them, and move on.


As the store grows, that same process starts creating unnecessary work. More products mean more images to create and update, more variants to manage, more seasonal changes, more opportunities for inconsistencies, and more files moving between Shopify and editing tools.


That is where the[Photoroom Shopify integration](https://www.photoroom.com/product-catalog/shopify) changes the workflow.


Once Shopify is connected, Photoroom imports the store's product images into a Shopify Products catalog. Sellers can work from those products directly, edit existing imagery, create new assets, manage visual variants, improve listing information, and publish supported changes back to Shopify.


**Your first 20 Shopify products may not need an image workflow. Your next 500 probably do.**


This guide explains how growing Shopify stores can use Photoroom to manage the product-image workflow from the connected catalog, from deciding what needs attention and editing images in bulk to creating new assets, managing variants, improving listings, and publishing updates back to Shopify.


## **How to manage your Shopify product-image workflow with Photoroom**


Once you connect your Shopify store to Photoroom, your existing product images are imported into Photoroom. From there, you can work on the imagery and supported listing information for your products without building a separate file-based workflow every time something needs to change.


Changes are saved in Photoroom first, so you can review your work before publishing approved updates back to Shopify.


Here’s how that works as your catalog grows.


### **1. Connect your Shopify store to Photoroom**


[Connect your Shopify store](https://www.photoroom.com/integrations/shopify) to bring your existing product catalog and imagery into Photoroom. This gives you a direct starting point for the rest of the workflow, without downloading product images from Shopify before you can edit or create new assets.


Instead of starting from folders of disconnected files, you start from the products already in your catalog.


### **2. Decide which Shopify products need attention**


A growing catalog doesn’t mean every product needs to be edited.


You might need to work on:


-


newly added products without a complete image set


-


older listings with inconsistent imagery


-


supplier images that need cleaning up


-


products that need new lifestyle or contextual images


-


color variants that need their own visuals


-


groups of products that need the same visual update


-


listings that are missing important images or information


Each connected Shopify product gets a[Listing Score](https://www.photoroom.com/product-catalog/listing-score) with recommended actions, such as adding more images. This gives you a quick way to see which products need attention and what to improve next.


The shift is important: **work from what the catalog needs, rather than treating every SKU as a new production project.**


### **3. Edit and prepare the product images you already have**


If the source imagery is accurate, you often don’t need to start again.


Inside Photoroom, you can work on existing Shopify product images by:


-


removing or replacing backgrounds


-


resizing images


-


repositioning the product


-


adjusting the composition


-


adding or replacing images


-


standardizing the visual treatment across products


You can also use[Photoroom’s AI tools](https://www.photoroom.com/tools) directly from the product workspace when a product needs more than a basic edit.


Depending on what you're selling and the image you need to create, you can use tools such as:


-


**Recolor**


-


**Product Beautifier**


-


**AI Fashion Models**


-


**Product Staging**


-


**Edit with AI**


-


**Flat Lay**


-


**Ghost Mannequin**


-


**Ironing**


-


**AI Scenes**


You don’t need every tool for every product: once the Shopify product is in Photoroom, you can choose the editing or AI workflow that fits the asset without moving it into another production process.


If the same treatment applies across many products, use[batch editing](https://www.photoroom.com/batch) instead of processing each image individually.


### **4. Create the additional product images your listing needs**


Once you have a reliable product image, you can use **AI Shot List** to create additional shots from the product imagery you already have.


AI Shot List can generate different product presentations such as:


-


front


-


back


-


side


-


detail


-


lifestyle


-


other relevant product shots


You can also provide multiple source images when more product information is needed for better accuracy.


This is particularly useful for a small Shopify seller because one product source can support a much richer listing without turning every missing visual into another photoshoot.


Start with the shopper question: **What does someone still need to see to understand this product?**


Then create the shots that can be generated reliably from the source imagery.


**Don’t generate more shots just because you can. Generate the shots that close a shopper information gap.**


Need to decide what images a new product listing should include? See[how to create all the product images a Shopify listing needs with AI.](https://www.photoroom.com/blog/how-small-shopify-sellers-can-create-all-the-product-images-a-listing-needs)


### **5. Create product images for Shopify variants**


If a product comes in multiple options, such as different colors or sizes, the variants themselves are created and managed in Shopify.


Photoroom helps you create and work on the imagery that represents those variants.


For suitable colorways, you can start from an accurate product image and create additional versions while maintaining a consistent presentation across the range.


For example, a product available in five colors can keep the same composition, primary-image treatment, and additional visual style while showing the correct purchasable option.


**Shopify manages the product variants. Photoroom helps you create and manage the imagery for them.**


If a variant also changes material, pattern, hardware, shape, or construction, use source imagery that captures those differences.


**Reuse the presentation. Preserve the product truth.**


### **6. Update groups of Shopify products when something changes**


The same connected workflow works for products that are already live.


You may want to:


-


introduce a new background across a category


-


bring older products in line with a new visual standard


-


clean up supplier imagery


-


refresh seasonal presentations


-


update products for a campaign


-


replace outdated imagery


If the product itself hasn’t changed, you don’t necessarily need to recreate the asset.


Update the part of the presentation that changed and apply repeated changes across the relevant products where possible.


**Update what changed. Don’t recreate what didn’t.**


### **7. Optimize the Shopify product title and description**


Once the imagery is ready, you can also work on the listing copy without leaving Photoroom.


For connected Shopify products, you can edit the existing title and description or generate new versions with AI.


This lets a small seller prepare both the visual and written parts of the listing in the same workflow instead of treating image creation, copywriting, and publishing as separate jobs.


Review generated copy for:


-


product accuracy


-


clarity


-


brand voice


-


useful shopper language


-


relevant search terms


### **8. Optimize image names and alt text for SEO**


Photoroom also lets you work on SEO metadata for the product images.


You can generate or edit:


-


**SEO-optimized image names**


-


**descriptive alt text**


That means image SEO doesn’t need to become another task after the visual work is finished.


Keep both accurate and descriptive. Don’t stuff filenames or alt text with keywords purely for SEO.


### **9. Review the product and recheck the listing**


Before publishing, check that edited or generated imagery still represents what the customer will receive.


Review:


-


color


-


shape and proportions


-


materials and texture


-


logos and labels


-


patterns and important details


-


correct variant assignment


For generated scenes, also check scale, perspective, lighting, and whether the product interacts naturally with its environment.


Then revisit the **Listing Score** to see whether the product still has recommended actions before publishing.


**Scale the production process, not the mistakes.**


### **10. Publish the approved changes back to Shopify**


Once the imagery and supported listing information are ready, publish the approved changes back to Shopify through the integration.


This closes the loop.


You don’t need to export a folder of finished assets, organize them, return to Shopify, find the correct products, upload everything again, and reconnect images with their listings.


The product stays at the center of the workflow from the moment you start working on it to the moment the update is published.


For a growing Shopify store, that’s the real advantage of connecting Photoroom to the catalog:


**you’re not just making individual image edits faster. You’re reducing the manual work around producing, improving, and maintaining the entire product listing as the catalog grows.**


## **What does this workflow look like for a two-person Shopify team?**


The sportswear brand[Layer](https://www.photoroom.com/customer-stories/layer) is run by a two-person team. Before using Photoroom, producing product imagery involved expensive photoshoots, manual editing, and uploading finished assets to Shopify. Individual photoshoots had cost the company more than £500 while still not producing all the imagery it wanted.


Layer using Photoroom to generate more product visuals from existing products


Layer now uses Photoroom to create studio-style product images, lifestyle scenes, model imagery, batch edits, and other creative assets in-house. With the Shopify integration, the team can also work with imagery already connected to its store and push finished images back to Shopify.


Co-founder Dan Bacon describes being able to find the Shopify images in Photoroom, edit them, and have them back on the website within minutes.


Layer reports a **50% increase in online sales** alongside the change in its visual-production workflow.


**A two-person e‑commerce team can manage a much richer product-image workflow without building a photography, editing, and catalog-production team around it.**


## **Use Photoroom to scale your Shopify product-image production**


As a Shopify store grows, product visuals stop being only an editing problem. It becomes part of how the[catalog](https://www.photoroom.com/product-catalog) is operated.


With Photoroom for Shopify, sellers can work from the products already in their store, edit individual or groups of assets, create missing imagery and variant visuals, improve listing information, identify incomplete listings, review the results, and publish supported changes back to Shopify.


For a small business, the real advantage is simple:


**more products without proportionally more manual image-production work.**


Your Shopify catalog can grow faster than the team managing its imagery.


**If product-image work is starting to slow your store down, connect Shopify to Photoroom and manage the workflow directly from your catalog.**
